# E5 — is the GPU working, or waiting for the CPU? (T007 step 1)

**Generated by `bench/make_e5_report.py` from the committed `results/*_E5_<model>_<mode>_timeline/` directories** (`bench/t007_timeline.py` on T006's nsys captures, two inferences each). Nothing here is typed in.

Definitions (as `reference/orin/bench/parse_nsys.py`): **wall** = the GPU-projected NVTX range in the nsys capture; **kernel union** = the union of kernel intervals inside it; **GPU idle** = wall − union. nsys tracing stretches ranges, so idle is also given against the untraced CUDA-event time of the same configuration's T005 row (**idle vs event** = 1 − union ÷ event time; negative values mean the traced kernels took longer than the event median, i.e. no measurable idle). Gaps between consecutive kernels are split: **intra-graph** (two nodes of one CUDA-graph launch), **CPU-starved** (the next kernel's launch call returned only after the previous kernel had finished: the GPU had nothing queued) and **queued** (work was submitted; launch latency or a device dependency). `ae_step` rows are the mean per denoising step over all steps of both inferences; other rows are per inference.

## Orin (labelled Orin; `reference/orin/reports/E5_timeline.md`, "Per region" table)

Orin's expert step was mostly GPU-idle when eager (π0 `eager` ae_step idle 84 %, corrected 76 %; π0.5 64 %, corrected 47 %) and still 45–47 % idle in its best π0 / π0.5 configuration; GR00T's compiled action head was ≈ 0.1 % idle (N1.5 / N1.6 / N1.7 `best` ae_total 0.08–0.10 %), while N1.7's eager vision and prefix were 42 % and 64 % idle. See that file for the full table.
